newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Poongsan wins Canberra coin-blanks deal.
newsitem.headline: Poongsan wins Canberra coin-blanks deal.

text.p: South Korea's Poongsan Corp has secured a US$17 million order order from the Australian government for the supply of 3,000 tonnes of coin-blanks over the next three years, the firm said on Thursday.

Poongsan said in a statement it would supply the Royal Australian Mint in Canberra with six kinds of blanks for five, 10, 20 and 50 cent coins which are made of cupro-nickel and for one and two Australian dollar coins made of alumnium bronze.
The supply contract starts this year and runs to 1999.
Poonsang said it had supplied about 2,000 tonnes of coin-blanks to the Australian government in the past two years.
The company expected additional sales as Australia also supplies coins to New Zealand, Papua New Guinea and the Republic of Fiji, it said.
Poonsang also expects orders for precious metal blanks for commemorative coins for the 2000 Sydney Olympic Games.
